inputs.text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court granted regular bail to a man booked under national-security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, based on allegations that he was in telephone contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri.” That is not an acquittal—but neither should a security label turn suspicion into proof. The call to ensure courts don’t leave “genuine security threats” free risks putting state anxieties ahead of basic rights. Governments must protect people by building credible cases and respecting due process, not by treating contact or association as guilt. Security laws need scrutiny precisely because unchecked state power can harm the people least able to defend themselves.
